label: text
text: Premier Asked About

label: text
text: STATEMENT IN PARLIAMENT.

label: paragraph_title
text: Canton Strikers Confident of

label: text
text: Beyond a statement that the matter had the attention of the Government, MS. Stanley Baldwin had nothing to say in Parliament yesterday on the settlement of the Canton boreott, pending the return of the British Foreign Minister to London.

label: text
text: There is little new to report since yesterday. In Canton the spirit of optimism prevails as to the outcome.

label: text
text: It is felt that communications will be restored by October 1, or next Monday at the latest, without interference, with the complete removal of the pickets.

label: text
text: Whether ships will be running again as usual remains to be seen. Predictions are that there will be no general start as soon as the boycott is lifted but that a gradual resumption will follow.

label: text
text:
London, Sept. 28.
In the House of Commons, a question by Mr. Pathick Lawrence elicited a further statement by Mr. Stanley Baldwin (Premier) regarding the general situation in China at the conclusion of which Mr. Ramsay MacDonald asked

label: text
text: Whether the Government had taken notice of the fiscal conditions attached to the removal of the boycott.

label: text
text: The Premier said that in the absence of Sir Austen Chamberlain (Foreign Secretary), who returns in a few days, all he could say was that the matter was at present engaging the Government's attention.]—Reufer.

label: text
text: Strikers in Canton are said to number anything between 10,000 and 50,000.

label: text
text: Should a bounty be paid, it is thought that applicants will not be over 20,000 at the utmost. The sum mentioned is either $50 in money or $100 in treasury bonds (now current at par).

label: text
text: Members of the rank and file are now coming to Hong Kong to seek employment before the final call-off.

label: text
text: A restaurant waiter of West Point told the "China Mail" an interesting story yesterday.

label: text
text: Getting Back to Normal.

label: text
text: He had been drawing 60 cents a month, with free meals and a bed in a Canton dormitory, ever since the strike began but had not taken up duty as a picket.

label: text
text: A tip "from those who knew" had reached him, "hence his trip to Hong Kong to secure employment after Oct. 1 and to rent a cubicle for his family. He came down on a pass for a week, which also included free passage on the Chinese section of the railway. It was his intention to return in a day or two to be present at the demobilisation in Canton "so that he would be square with everybody."

label: paragraph_title
text: 90 Per Cent. Belief.

label: text
text: The most interesting part was that many other strikers who had heard the same news were “90 percent... certain” that the boycott would be over and they were all coming down to look around.

label: text
text: Quicer tales are associated with the name of Tam Hoi-shan, now chairman of one of the Strike Committees. Previously he had hawked shoes in West Point and went by the name of "Shoe" Po. "People who had called him that in Canton had been thrown into prison. "Tam Po" was deemed a term of insult. The least that he condemned to be addressed by was "Tam old four," "Mr. Tam Hoi-shan" or "Head of Bureau Tam" was preferred.

label: text
text: Pickets and Their Boats.

label: text
text: The strike pickets at the East (French) bridge have now been withdrawn.

label: text
text: The gate at the bridge has been opened: Chinese and foreigners are passing through freely.

label: text
text: All motor launches used by Strike Pickets are to be completely handed over to the Police Department and they will be used by the Water Police for river patrols—"Wah Taz Yat Po"

label: paragraph_title
text: FEARS ALLAYED.

label: text
text: MACAO FISHING FLEET WHEREABOUTS.

label: text
text: Fears for the safety of the Macao fishing fleet with about 2,000 people on board have been allayed to a considerable extent by further inquiries.

label: text
text: Although caught at sea, the greater majority of the boats fled to shelter in time, or rode out the storm, their uncanny knowledge of neighbouring waters standing them in good stead.

label: text
text: It was because most of the boats did not put back at Macao on Tuesday morning that alarm was first felt.

label: text
text: Few of the boats sank, but quite a number of the junkes were severely buffetted by wind and wave.

label: text
text: There was little damage other than detailed in yesterday's "China Mail."

label: text
text: On shore, the effects are no worse than in Hong Kong.

label: text
text:
From An Occasional Correspondent.]
Morgan Set 29

label: text
text: Some of the fishing boats have returned and others put in at Cheung Chau Island (Hong Kong waters) after the storm.

label: text
text: A number had their masts carried away. Other junks cut their masts, sail and gear to save the hull and were successful.

label: text
text: A few have been damaged but not beyond repair. Anxiety is now only felt.for those that may have lagged behind after failing to make port early on Monday morning.

label: text
text: There were two outstanding disasters.

anchored there the previous

label: text
text: There was another up-river boat which suddenly capsized. All 27 people on board perished.

label: paragraph_title
text: EURASIAN KILLED.

label: paragraph_title
text: POLICE ARRIVAL CAUSES PANIC.

label: text
text: A young Eurasian named Alfred Cunningham, who was a salesman at Messrs. Brunner Mond and Company, Ltd. and lived with his parents at Robinson Road, met his death under sad circumstances last night.

label: text
text: It was stated in a report that police officers were endeavouring to arrest him on a warrant. Information having been received that he was to be found at Yu On Terrace, West Point (below the mortuary), a party of police went there shortly before midnight. Their presence becoming known to the deceased, it is presumed that he jumped out of a window on the third floor (the Tin Tin club) in an endeavour to escape.

label: text
text: When the officers later entered the lane into which he fell they found the head badly battered and severe injuries to the upper part of the body. It is believed that death must have been instantaneous.

label: text
text: The late Mr. Cunningham was one of those who was commended by Mr. D. Burlingham (Deputy Superintendent of Police) for assistance given in the rescuing alive of a Chinese girl who was imprisoned for 40 hours in the debris at the Po Hing Fong disaster last year.

label: paragraph_title
text: THE WEATHER

label: text
text: The forecast until noon tomorrow is east winds, fresh; fine to cloudy.

label: text
text: Remarks in Observatory report to-day are as under:—

label: text
text: Depression or typhoon in Lat. 17 N. Long. 116 E., direction unknown, position uncertain.

label: text
text: Pressure has increased moderately at Vladivostok and slightly over Japan. Formosa, the Philippine and Indo-China. The anticyclone has moved quickest eastward. There may be a typhoonial the Macles fields, probably missing westward but this is uncertain at present.

label: paragraph_title
text: LINES IN DANGER.

label: paragraph_title
text: Cantonese Pushed Out of

label: paragraph_title
text: Kiangsi.

label: text
text: SUN CHUAN-FANG ADVANCING.

label: text
text:
Allies Now Marching on Hankow-
Canton Railway.

label: text
text: Canton's line of communications between Hankow and Canton is now in danger as Sun Chuan-fang's allies are rapidly marching out of Kiangsi into Hunan province.

label: text
text: Following the recapture of Nanchang, the allies have kept up their counter-offensive.

label: text
text: In the north of Kiangsi, they drove back the 3rd army under General Chu Pei-teh and the 1st Army (mostly Cadets) under Lt.-Gen. Wang Pah-ling.

label: text
text: The southerners' line is still in the form of a semi-circle but the allies have bent back the flanks and pushed the centre back (westwards, towards Yochow and Wuchang) for some considerable distance.

label: text
text: At the moment, the allies (advancing both from Kiangsi and Anhui) are moving forwards and not far from the northern section of the Hankow-Canton Railway.

label: text
text: Further south, the allies have also advanced, the 3rd and 6th armies retiring to preserve the alignment.

label: text
text: General Teng Ju-cho (tupan of Kiangsi) is now endeavouring to push the southerners out of the south of Kiangsi.

label: text
text: On this part of the line, the Nationalists are still fairly secure.

label: text
text: Miss Scarlett, the lady missionary from Kongmoon, has been recovered by H.M.S. "Robin" and the Customs launch "Kongmoon Chai" has also been brought back, but a European officer is still missing. See report in shipping section on page 4.

label: text
text: Training times by local race ponies will be found on page 9, sports section.

label: text
text: tory are advancing by way of the Yangtse River. Should any break through towards Wuchang, then the southerners may have to make a precipitate retreat.

label: text
text: On the other hand, a part of the Nationalist Army is still moving northwards, from Hankow, in pursuit of Wu Pei-fu whose troops are not doing very much just now.

label: paragraph_title
text: ON THREE FRONTS.

label: text
text: It is also reported that the southerners are advancing beyond Sinyangchów towards Chu-ma-tien.

label: text
text: Considerable bodies. of troops are coming from the upper Yangtse to Shasi and possibly beyond (i.e., further down river towards Hankow?).—Official despatch.

label: text
text: Without an explanation the above despatch may be misleading. As it is, it is full of possibilities and shows the Nationalists to be in danger of being cut off.

label: text
text:
The “China Mail” special correspondent has already reported that the “5 province” allies were pushing out of the northern corner of Kiangsi province. Huang ski-kang is on the Yangtse, in Hunan province (controlled by the southerners) and Tayeh is even nearer to Wuchang. That is to say, Sun Chuan-fang has already moved from Kiukiang, in a westerly direction, and has now occupied territory recently held by the Cantonese. Sun Chuan-fang's holding of Tayeh may mean a serious threat at the southerners' line between Hankow and Canton.

text: A British tug was fired at, whe off Hanyang (near Hankow) thiorning.

text: The B., and S., s. Wanhien arrived at Ichang today (Tues day).—Official despatch.

text: Peking, Sept., 22.

label: text
text: The military authorities at Kiukiang (Sun Chuan-fang's) have issued a notification requiring the Chinese Maritime Customs to search vessels and close the port from midnight to six o'clock in the morning, but it is not certain from the telegrams received in Peking whether this is intended to apply to foreign vessels.

label: text
text: H.M.S. "Woodcock" and Japanese gunboat are at praser stationed at Kiukiang.

label: text
text: The troops coming down the Yangtse towards Shasi are those of Yang Sen and other pro-Wu Pei-fu-ites, who are marching down to assist Wu Pei-fu.

Gen. Chl Hsieh-yuan (Wu Pei-fu's right-hand man) who returned to Changhsintien yesterday evening after a conference with the Fengtien authorities at Peking, will probably proceed to Chengchow shortly to consult Wu Peifu about sending. Fengtien reinforcements to the South.—

Reuter.

label: paragraph_title
text: REPORTS BY MAIL

label: paragraph_title
text: Nancheng's Fall—And Recapture.

label: text
text: A wireless from KiuKiang received this morning says, that according to the Chief of Police who fled from Nanchang and arrived there at 9 p.m., Nanchang was captured by 1,500. southern troops under command of General Chu Fei-teh, with whom the garrison stationed there as well as a larger number of students sided. The routed troops and rioters set fire to the houses in one part of the city, following the looting.

label: text
text:
Troops Surrounded.
General Teng Ju-cho's troops
were enveloped by the Cantonese
at Changshu, several miles downstream of Linkiang.

label: text
text: Upon arrival at Kiuklang, Marshall Sun Chuan-fang held a military conference. As a consequence, the Generals who participated set out for their posts on Sept. 22: A decisive battle against the southerners is expected to take place shortly.

label: text
text: The progress of a battle in the direction of "Lohuu is reported to be in favour" of the Allied forces.

label: text
text: There is a tendency among the inhabitants of Kiukiang to welcome the arrival of the southern troops, while the higher class is afraid of the invasion. Wild rumours are current in the city, following the entry of the Southerners' propagandists.—Shanghai Mercury.

label: text
text: Kukiang, Sept. 22.

label: text
text: Though Nanchang had fallen into the hands of southern troops for a time owing to the defeat of the Kiaugsi troops, Marshal Sun Chuan-fang's forces, which took the offensive, have now practically re-captured Nanchang, after very severe fighting. The southern troops, numbering some 3,000, are now in a fix in the delta below Nanchang.—Toho.

label: text
text:
Chang's Movements.
Peking, Sept. 22.
General Chang Kai-shek arrived at Changsha from Wuchang on Sept. 18, and went on to Liling and Pinghejiang.

label: text
text: It is reported that he will direct an offensive against Nanchang.

label: text
text: Kukiang is full of rumours many of an alarmist nature and many rich people are moving their belongings from the native city into the foreign concession, and some of them are leaving themselves for Shanghai or elsewhere.

label: paragraph_title
text: RUDDERLESS.

label: text
text:
Typhoon and B. & S.
Boat.

label: text
text: MORE JUNK DEATHS.

label: paragraph_title
text: Incoming Steamers Bring Many Refugees.

label: text
text: A breakdown in her steering gear, due to the typhoon of which she sustained the full force, was experienced by the B. and S. steamer (China Navigation Company). "Kweiyang" on its way to Hong Kong. The vessel was held up off Gap Rock powerless to make port until towed in by the Kowloon Dock Salvage tug, the "Henry Keswick." After going to the quarantine anchorage, the "Kweiyang" proceeded to her buoy.

label: text
text: It is not anticipated that the damage will necessitate the vessel leaving the buoy for the necessary repairs to be carried out.

label: text
text: Among the passengers were the "Globe Trotters" whose performance at the "Star" had of necessity to be postponed again until to-night.

label: text
text: Junk Refugees.

label: text
text: The many refugees from fishing junks and small vessels temporarily accommodated in quarters adjoining the harbour office give to the vicinity the appearance of a clearance hospital.

label: text
text: Many of the refugees were in a pitiful plight at the time they were landed, having been without food since the typhoon struck them. Others are suffering from the after-effects of their struggle with the elements, complaining of fever and headaches.

label: text
text: Meanwhile, reports continue to be received of loss of life aboard junk at sea when the typhoon arrived.

label: paragraph_title
text: Wrecked Off Lima

label: text
text:
Three fishing junka were wrecked during the typhoon of Lima Island. Each junk had an approximate crew of 14 persons, and of the total there are 16 survivors. Although those saved saw some of their companions clinging to their wrecked junks they hold out little hope as to their having been saved.
Nevertheless, they have asked the help of the Harbour Master to find the rest of the crew, and at 1 p.m. to-day, a rescue tug was despatched under the command of Boarding Officer Thompson to the scene of disaster.

label: paragraph_title
text: Rescue by s.s. "Kochow."

label: text
text: One of the several junks which broke away from their moorings at Shamshuipo drifted. in the direction of the s.s. "Kochow" and all the occupants, fourteen men and three women, were saved by the crew of the vessel. The fate of the junk, No. 2060, is unknown. Three junks are ashore at Stonecutter's Island. Junk No. 2619 is lying high and dry on the beach. No. 5102 is a total wreck. Six Chinese were rescued from this boat. The third is an unknown junk and had no occupants on board when a rescue party went there.

label: paragraph_title
text: Two Days Aflont.

label: text
text: The s.s. "Wing Wo," while underway to Hong Kong from Kwong-chow-wan, picked 4 fishermen whose respective junks had sunk during the typhoon, and who were the sole survivors. The refugees had been in the water for two days, without sleep, food nor shelter.

label: text
text: The s.s. "Yei Maru", Capt. Yagi commanding, also picked up four fishermen at about 10 a.m. yesterday morning about 8 miles from Gap Rock.

label: text
text: According to a report made by the master of the Naval oil tanker "Francol" the crew of the vessel saved two men from a fishing junk which was then about 25 miles south-east of Hong Kong. Those rescued stated that the junk carried a crew of 27 persons. From a later report it was ascertained that there were seven survivors from the ill-fated junk (No. 3183). The remaining twenty are believed to have been drowned.

label: text
text: Two fatalities are reported on a fishing junk which was at Ping Hoy when it capsized in a heavy sea, throwing four persons into the water. Another boat picked up two of the men in an exhausted condition and brought them to Hong Kong.
